originalBehavior: Original local implementation: meaningful watch assemblies are modeled separately from physical source mesh templates.
localStatus: The workbench validates 71 unique semantic components against the 85-entry binary mesh table, creates source-backed and procedural geometry, preserves the mainplate as the datum, and restores archived local offsets and ZYX rotation order for 16 pivot-sensitive source meshes.
notes: Semantic assemblies carry user-facing names, roles, systems, mounting positions, and animation labels.
Pivot-sensitive hands, power, train, escapement, and balance meshes retain archived source-local offsets, flips, and ZYX rotation composition after per-source AABB centering.
The raw table retains all 85 templates for source accountability without presenting each template as an installed watch component.
evidence: The WebGL canvas exposes data-component-count=71 after successful initialization.
Source references are validated before renderer initialization and invalid ranges fail fast.

originalBehavior: Original local implementation: one problem, one mechanism, and one visible result explain each module in a causal sequence.
localStatus: Ten ordered lessons isolate Power, Gear Train, Escapement, Balance, Mainplate, Click, Motion Works, Keyless Works, Automatic Winding, and Physical Scale while retaining the mainplate as a quiet datum.
notes: Lesson progression updates explanatory copy, active semantic assemblies, camera focus, register rows, and selected part as one state change.
Relevant components separate only along their mounting axes; unrelated assemblies become inactive and disappear.
evidence: The guide exposes ten lesson buttons with aria-current on the active step and a 01 / 10 progress counter.
The Power lesson exposes four register parts, then Next lesson changes the scene and explanation to Gear Train.

originalBehavior: Original local implementation: service order, full-part navigation, and mechanical motion remain available after the guided explanation.
localStatus: A secondary Explore complete movement disclosure exposes Service, Atlas, and Energy views. Service assembles along mounting axes, Atlas arranges seven territories, and Energy sends animated torque through regulation, hour, minute, and seconds branches.
notes: Each mode has an authored camera pose; free orbit is opt-in and Reset view restores the authored framing.
Reduced-motion preference pauses startup animation and makes position transitions immediate; settled paused scenes stop requesting frames.
evidence: Atlas mode exposes seven projected territory labels and sets data-mode=atlas on the WebGL canvas.
Energy mode marks the torque-path assemblies in the component register and updates the animated scene while playing.

originalBehavior: Original local implementation with neutral provenance and no upstream runtime embed.
localStatus: The page uses a route-local responsive shell, the sibling vendored Three.js modules, local binary assets, and the shared public footer.
notes: The archived mechanical-watch base.js and watch.js runtime are not loaded by this route.
Desktop keeps one bounded lesson surface; tablet and mobile stack the explanation, canvas, lesson rail, register, and inspector without horizontal overflow.
The lesson brief and part detail are aria-atomic; setLesson updates five sibling nodes and showPart replaces the detail subtree, so partial announcements were possible without it.
The subsystem filter container exposes role=group alongside its existing aria-label so its generated pressed buttons form a named group.
evidence: smoke-bundle.mjs --route watch-mesh-explorer passes desktop and mobile baselines.
Targeted smoke asserts aria-atomic=true on .lesson-brief and [data-part-detail], and role=group plus the accessible name on div.system-filter.
